back: The title of the ruler of the Mutapa state, usually explained as "lord of the conquered lands".
A large estate in the Zambezi valley leased by the Portuguese Crown to settlers (prazeros), who ruled over African inhabitants.

front: Who were the traditional founders of the Mutapa state?
back: Mutota and his son Matope, in the fifteenth century.

front: When did the Portuguese take Sofala?
What happened to Gonçalo da Silveira in 1561?
back: The Jesuit missionary, who had baptised the Mutapa, was killed at his court.

front: Which Mutapa ruler made a treaty with the Portuguese in 1607?
Why did the Mutapa state expand?
back: Conquest by Mutota and Matope, tribute, the gold and ivory trade, religious authority and a fertile Zambezi valley base.

front: Give four reasons for the decline of the Mutapa state.
back: Succession disputes and civil war, Portuguese interference, the break-away of provinces, and the rise of the Rozvi.

front: How did spirit mediums support Mutapa rulers?
back: They spoke for the royal ancestors, helped to legitimise a ruler and could influence who succeeded.
